name: UFP Industries Inc
business: UFP Industries makes treated lumber, composite decking, pallets, packaging and engineered framing components for home-improvement retailers, builders and industrial customers.

events.what: CEO succession (internal); Matthew Missad to Executive Chairman. Effective date is outside the 18-month window (cutoff 2025-04-01)
Bolt-on acquisition: MoistureShield composite decking plant, $55M cash (2025 sales about $50M)
Bolt-on acquisition: John Rock pallets, $47M cash (2025 sales about $86M)
Bolt-on acquisition: Berry Pallets, $20M cash (2025 sales about $23M)
New EVP Operations Integration role (internal, from President of Construction segment); not an Item 5.02 officer change

next_event.source: Lexical 'investor day' search over FY2026 calls found nothing; 8-K 2026-07-29 says long-term goals 'remain unchanged'. The $60M cost-out program ends 2026-12-31; FY2026 results (early 2027) are the next checkpoint.

margin_framing.metric_basis_note: Two numeric frames. (1) A 12.5% adjusted EBITDA margin long-term goal with no target year, repeated by CEO Schwartz and in each 2026 earnings release. Baba shows it first in the Q4 2023 call (document_id 91814, Missad, 'stretched goal'; date not fetched), so it predates the new CEO. (2) A $60M cost-out (half SG&A, half capacity consolidation) 'by the end of 2026', set at the beginning of 2025; CFO Cole says $35M SG&A plus $7M capacity was done in 2025 and a further $25M comes in 2026. The caller's 'stated 2027 margin targets' could not be found: lexical '2027' over FY2026 documents returns only decking capacity and packaging comments, no margin target.

statements.quote: reminder, we are driving towards the following goals: A 12.5% EBITDA margin, 7%-10% unit sales growth, some of it which will come from M&A and new products.

statements.quote: With these objectives in mind, we set a goal at the beginning of 2025 to achieve $60 million of cost reductions by the end of 2026, with half coming from SG&A and the other half coming from capacity consolidations that reduce our cost of goods sold.

statements.quote: On the cost side, we are actively mitigating higher costs and remain on track to deliver the remaining $25 million of our $60 million cost-out program by year-end, with the potential to capture incremental savings beyond our initial targets.

statements.quote: The company's long-term goals remain unchanged and include: 1) achieving 7-10 percent unit sales growth annually (including bolt-on acquisitions) with at least 10 percent of all sales coming from new products; 2) achieving 12.5 percent adjusted EBITDA margins;
statements.speaker: Press release

street.gap_assumption: Calendar fiscal year, Baba labels match. No target year for 12.5%, so the gap uses FY2028, the last consensus year with data (FY2029 is empty). Same metric on both sides (adjusted EBITDA over net sales). Only 5 brokers. The $60M cost-out is about 95 bps on FY2026 consensus sales but is largely already in the run-rate.
street.source: Baba data_financials consensus (Visible Alpha), summary and fundamentals

evidence_of_progress.note: Order [Q1 2026, Q2 2026]. Q1 7.62% vs 8.91% (Baba actuals; CFO confirmed 7.6% vs 8.9%, document_id 180268). Q2 8.22% vs 9.49%: $154.5M on $1.88B (rounded, 8-K 0000912767-26-000044) vs Baba actual $174.15M on $1,835.4M. H1 2026 adjusted EBITDA margin 7.9% per the 8-K. Margin keeps falling despite about $42M of cost-out already done; Site Built pricing, transportation costs and housing are swamping savings. Lumber price moves also shift the margin denominator, so part of any recovery would be commodity-driven.

disqualifier_reason: Catalyst older than 18 months with no pending change: the internal CEO succession was effective 2024-12-29 (21 months ago, before the 2025-04-01 cutoff), the CFO is unchanged, and the only in-window events are $122M of tuck-in acquisitions (about 3% of market cap). Margin is also partly lumber-price and housing-cycle driven.
verdict: Big gap but stale catalyst: 12.5% target vs 9.2% FY2028 consensus and a dated $60M cost-out, yet the internal CEO is 21 months in, margins are still falling, and nothing new is scheduled.
open_questions: Will management ever put a year on 12.5%, or will it reset the framework once the $60M program ends in December 2026?
How much of the 130 bps yearly margin decline is Site Built pricing and freight (cyclical) versus lost share (structural)?
Does the roughly $1.9B liquidity and 'meaningful M&A' language point to a transformational deal that would restart the catalyst clock?
